flow.title: Product flow
flow.lead: An agent reads only what this folder records and writes what the product is and how it moves. It does not read the source.
flow.actionHint: Puts this request in the conversation beside Analysis. You send it.
flow.checking: Checking which local agent can open here.
flow.requestLabel: The request that goes to the agent
flow.unavailableBody: A browser cannot start a process, so no agent launches here. Paste “The request that goes to the agent” into the terminal you already use and you get the same answer.
flow.noVaultBody: There is no vault to explain yet.
flow.request:
Use only Atlas MCP read tools to explain this ontology's business flow. Never call shell, file, source, web, or other tools.

Return exactly six ### headings with one paragraph each:
1) Why this product exists.
2) Which domains own which responsibilities.
3) How the main capabilities form a business flow.
4) How those capabilities appear in elements or paths.
5) Which declared dependencies explain impact, and what remains unknown.
6) Which partial, visible-gap, stale, or unverified limits must be retained.

Rules:
- Inspect the project map first and choose one representative meaning-to-implementation chain; do not enumerate every node.
- Read at most 12 concepts with get_concept(body: full) or get_concepts(body: full).
- Every paragraph names an exact full node slug whose complete body was read this turn.
- Write a from --type--> to relation only when it exists in the current ontology.
- Keep partial, visible-gap, and unknown qualifiers throughout.
- A capability's excludes bound that capability only; do not widen them to project scope.
- If the ontology cannot answer, say why instead of filling the gap from other knowledge.
